user_direction.summary: Disperse the six wind-carried sparks instead of letting them converge in a tight group. Alternate at least three clearly different horizontal speed bands, vary launch timing and altitude, and give two sparks stronger, phase-shifted crosswind motion. Keep each path curved, non-uniform, and independently timed.
user_direction.additional_feedback: The post-glow darkening made the SGDK contour merge into the dark field, reducing the apparent sharpness of the lettering. Preserve a crisp blue outline after the background settles to black.
user_direction.quality_feedback: The previous v003 still looked too clumped. The trajectories shared near-identical timing and converged at x=284..300. The dark blue contour also lost definition against the blackening field.
user_direction.skill_feedback: Scene direction did not set a measurable particle-separation target or post-fade logo-edge contrast target. Record as a local art-direction/cutscene handoff deficiency and candidate for revision; do not change the shared skill automatically.

rejected_previous_iteration.observed_runtime: The sweep executed, but read as monotonous and did not meet the agreed wind-carried energy.
rejected_previous_iteration.implementation_gap: Seven single sprites used separate quadratic positions but cycled sprite-sheet frames by global frame/index. There was no birth/active/fade profile, separate core and trail, per-instance flicker, or authored shrink/cooling phase.

visual_role: A short, airy glint across SGDK/FORGE that adds motion without becoming a solid bar or reducing wordmark readability.

trajectory_model.easing: smoothstep(t) = t*t*(3 - 2*t); each particle has an independent lifetime and distinct path handles.
trajectory_model.path: Each particle has a separate cubic path. Launch origins and endpoints occupy distinct horizontal and vertical positions. Paths may rise, dip, or lose altitude; no shared endpoint.

noise.sample: index = (floor(age / noise_period_frames) + noise_phase) modulo 16; x uses index + 6
noise.policy: spark_2 and spark_4 use amplitude 2 with distinct phase and period; the remaining particles use amplitude 1. Suppress noise for the first two and final two frames.

trajectory_model.runtime_policy: Integer-only deterministic motion. No gravity acceleration, heap, random state, alpha blend, hardware scaling, H-Int, per-frame tile upload, or sprite multiplexing. Reuse preloaded indexed sprite frames.

flicker.policy: Single-frame lower-luma flares on per-spark periods. Two sparks stay steady; no global synchronized pulse.

fade_out.apparent_shrink: Indexed sprite coverage reduces to a small dim core before the link is hidden. This is a discrete 8x8 pixel approximation; the VDP does not scale sprites.

directional_trail.source: Existing sprite strip frames 2/3/4, selected from horizontal/rising/falling path direction.
directional_trail.lag_px: Per-particle 4-5px behind the core along the local trajectory tangent.
directional_trail.depth: Trail links are explicitly behind their core links.

particle_lifecycle.glow: Use existing indexed bloom shapes and bright palette ramp. This is discrete pixel glow, not real blur or alpha.

budget_contract.measurement_required: Measure all 30 sweep frames for H40 count, width, links, and pairwise core separation.
budget_contract.headroom_justification: Six sparks are the authored direction target; paired trails use more links to make motion readable. Keep the mark dominant and judge pressure from measured paths.

acceptance_checks: The six lights read as separate wind-carried sparks, not one continuous bar.
Launch positions, timing, arcs, and speeds remain visibly asynchronous.
Each life starts softly, has a readable bright phase, and cools down while slowing and shrinking.
Trails follow local direction without covering the SGDK/FORGE lettering.
The frame sequence is clear on 320x224 BlastEm output and H40 geometry remains legal.

blastem_runtime_capture.capture_method: ffmpeg x11grab of the visible emulator window
blastem_runtime_capture.limitations: The capture shows the timed Splash V3 and spark passage, but is not frame-marked ROM-side and does not establish sustained FPS, audio quality, whole-scene VDP budget, or final visual acceptance.

logo_edge_contrast.problem: Dark blue outline indices became hard to distinguish while the PAL0 field faded to black.
logo_edge_contrast.rule: Raise only the three existing authored contour colors through the SGDK palette at the start of the backdrop fade. Keep the face palette and source pixels unchanged.
logo_edge_contrast.acceptance: At the black-field hold, the letter silhouette remains crisp and the three blue contour levels remain visible against black without a broad glow.

fallback.trigger: Core separation falls below 20px, paths appear parallel or mechanically synchronized, H40 limits are exceeded, or the blue contour still merges into the black field.
fallback.action: Retune only the six authored trajectory records and PAL1 contour values, then remeasure and replay the isolated candidate.

visual_review_note: The user reports that v003 particles still appear too clustered and that the SGDK outline loses definition as the blue field darkens. v004 adds three measured speed bands, staggered lifetimes, six spatially distinct paths, two stronger phase-shifted crosswind paths, and a staged contour palette lift. This remains a review candidate until the exact ROM is observed and accepted.

measurement_reconciliation.details: The previous v004 offline contract had different Y handles for two sparks than the C source captured in that ROM. Its 23.54px value described that contract, not the exact runtime geometry. V005 copies all trajectory fields from the C source and compares every active lifetime coordinate with the extracted C reference.
